cases.label: the oracle's reply
cases.reply: About 7 days. Arbitrum One's block.number approximates Ethereum L1 blocks, about 12 seconds each.

cases.label: a week
cases.reply: Roughly a week, because block.number there is the Ethereum block number.

cases.label: in seconds
cases.reply: 604,800 seconds. That's 50,400 blocks of 12 seconds, since a contract on Arbitrum sees L1 block numbers.

cases.label: in hours
cases.reply: 168 hours. Arbitrum's block.number follows Ethereum's blocks, not its own.

cases.label: just over 7 days
cases.reply: Just over 7 days, since block.number follows L1 and some L1 slots are missed.

cases.label: a range
cases.reply: 7-8 days. Arbitrum's block.number reports Ethereum's block number, about 12 s apart.

cases.label: opens with "The"
cases.reply: The vote stays open for about 7 days, because block.number on Arbitrum tracks L1 blocks.

cases.label: sets 3.5 hours apart
cases.reply: About 7 days, not the 3.5 hours you'd get from Arbitrum's quarter-second blocks, because block.number returns the L1 block number.

cases.label: names 3.5 hours in brackets
cases.reply: 7 days (or about 3.5 hours if it counted L2 blocks).

cases.label: a real reply (GPT)
cases.reply: **About 7 days.** On Arbitrum One, `block.number` tracks Ethereum L1 blocks rather than L2 blocks, so 50,400 × roughly 12 seconds is approximately one week.

cases.label: a real reply (Opus)
cases.reply: **About 7 days.** On Arbitrum One, `block.number` returns an approximation of the Ethereum L1 block number rather than the L2 block number, so 50,400 blocks × ~12 seconds per L1 block ≈ 604,800 seconds, or one week (the L2 block count would have given only a few hours).

cases.label: a real reply (Kimi)
cases.reply: **About 7 days.** On Arbitrum One, `block.number` tracks the Ethereum L1 block number at roughly 12 seconds per block, so 50,400 blocks equals about 604,800 seconds.

cases.label: a real reply (3.5 hours)
cases.reply: About 3.5 hours. Arbitrum One’s `block.number` advances by roughly one L2 block every 0.25 seconds, so 50,400 blocks is about 12,600 seconds.

cases.label: 3.5 hours
cases.reply: About 3.5 hours, since Arbitrum makes a block every 0.25 seconds.

cases.label: another duration
cases.reply: About 14 hours, at roughly one Arbitrum block per second.

cases.label: hedges
cases.reply: Either about 7 days or about 3.5 hours, depending on which block number the Governor reads.

cases.label: 7 days on L1, 3.5 hours on Arbitrum
cases.reply: About 7 days on Ethereum mainnet, but on Arbitrum One it's about 3.5 hours.

cases.label: contradicts itself
cases.reply: About 7 days. Arbitrum blocks come every 0.25 seconds, so 50,400 of them last about 3.5 hours.

cases.label: no duration
cases.reply: It depends on network activity, so there's no fixed duration.
